title: Why Are Some People Always Late? The Cultural Meaning of Time
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: the quality of arriving or doing things at the scheduled time
relating to or arranged in a straight line; sequential
occurring in repeated cycles; circular in pattern
a plan that lists activities or events and the times they will happen
the practice of doing several tasks at the same time
focused on or directed toward a particular goal, time, or attitude
a situation in which something is interpreted or understood incorrectly

sentences.en: You are invited to a party. The invitation says the party starts at 20:00.
sentences.zh: 你受邀去参加一个派对，邀请函上写着派对在晚上八点开始。

sentences.en: What time will you arrive? Your answer to this question has a lot to do with your culture.
sentences.zh: 你会在几点到？你对这个问题的回答很大程度上与你的文化背景有关。

sentences.en: Some of you will have said 20:00 exactly, because that is when the part stats.
sentences.zh: 你们当中有些人可能会说正好八点，因为派对就是那个时候开始的。

sentences.en: Others will have said 19:45, because it is polite to be early.
sentences.zh: 还有些人可能会说七点四十五，因为早到显得有礼貌。

sentences.en: Others will have said 20:30… or 21:00… or later because it is awkward to arrive too early.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则会说八点半……或者九点……甚至更晚，因为到得太早会很尴尬。

sentences.en: Your answer to my question is connected to how your culture understands time: the direction of time; the use time; punctuality; and more So today I want to look at the cultural meanings of time, highlight some common cultural misunderstandings that will be relevant for any of you living/studying/or working internationally, and do all of this while introducing new English vocabulary and practicing your English listening comprehension.
sentences.zh: 你对我这个问题的回答，与你所在的文化如何理解时间息息相关：时间的流逝方向、时间的运用、守时等等。所以今天我想探讨时间的文化含义，剖析一些常见的文化误解——这对于在国际间生活、学习或工作的各位都会很有帮助——同时引入新的英文词汇并练习大家的英语听力理解。

sentences.en: What exactly is time? This is not an easy question to answer.
sentences.zh: 时间到底是什么？这是一个不容易回答的问题。

sentences.en: Time has been theorized by scientists including Einstein and Newton.
sentences.zh: 包括爱因斯坦和牛顿在内的科学家们都曾对时间进行过理论探讨。

sentences.en: It has been debated by philosophers who like to discuss whether the past and future actually exist.
sentences.zh: 哲学家们也一直在争论过去和未来是否真的存在。

sentences.en: But for most of you listening, time is just seconds, minutes, hours.
sentences.zh: 但对收听节目的绝大多数人来说，时间不过是秒、分、时。

sentences.en: It’s something we measure with clocks or with our watch and with our calendars.
sentences.zh: 它是我们用时钟、手表或日历去度量的东西。

sentences.en: Time is so much more than this, though. It’s not a fixed universal system.
sentences.zh: 不过，时间的意义远不止于此。它并不是一个固定且普适的系统。

sentences.en: I just finished listening to the audiobook of the novel “Project Hail Mary” by Andy Weir, which has recently become a very successful Hollywood movie.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚听完了安迪·威尔（Andy Weir）的小说《挽救计划》（Project Hail Mary）的有声书，这部作品最近改编成了好莱坞大热电影。

sentences.en: I’ll try not to spoil the plot, but in the story the human character meets an alien species and they don’t experience time in the same way.
sentences.zh: 我会尽量不剧透，但在故事中，人类主角遇到了一种外星物种，而他们体验时间的方式并不一样。

sentences.en: They have to find a common time. One minute is 25 seconds in the Aliens time system.
sentences.zh: 他们必须找到一个共同的时间标准。在外星人的时间系统里，一分钟只有25秒。

sentences.en: One Earth Day is equivalent to 4 days 5,100 seconds in the alien system.
sentences.zh: 一个地球日相当于外星系统里的4天又5100秒。

sentences.en: So these characters have to come to some kind of agreement.
sentences.zh: 所以这些角色必须达成某种协议。

sentences.en: They have to understand each other’s time.
sentences.zh: 他们必须理解彼此的时间概念。

sentences.en: And that really just showed me, reinforced to me, that time is not a fixed thing.
sentences.zh: 这真的向我展示并加深了我的认识，即时间并不是一个固定不变的东西。

sentences.en: It’s a social construct. It’s something that we have decided.
sentences.zh: 它是一个社会建构。它是我们共同决定的产物。

sentences.en: Different cultures think about and use time differently.
sentences.zh: 不同的文化对时间的思考和运用方式各不相同。

sentences.en: Project Hail Mary is an extreme example, but there are much clearer examples.
sentences.zh: 《挽救计划》是一个极端的例子，但现实中有更明显的例子。

sentences.en: For instance, in some countries, time is treated like money.
sentences.zh: 例如，在某些国家，时间被当作金钱对待。

sentences.en: People talk about “saving time “, “wasting time “, “spending time “.
sentences.zh: 人们会谈论“节省时间”、“浪费时间”、“度过时间”。

sentences.en: Life is organized around a schedule or a deadline.
sentences.zh: 生活是围绕着日程表或截止日期来安排的。

sentences.en: And you shouldn’t be late. You should attend things on time or early.
sentences.zh: 你不应该迟到。你应该准时或提前参加活动。

sentences.en: But in other parts of the world, especially many African or Middle Eastern cultures, parts of Latin America as well, time is so much more flexible.
sentences.zh: 但在世界的其他地方，尤其是许多非洲、中东文化以及拉丁美洲的部分地区，时间要灵活得多。

sentences.en: People tend to prioritize their relationships or their experiences more than the schedule.
sentences.zh: 人们往往把人际关系或亲身经历看得比日程安排更重要。

sentences.en: So in these cultures, being on time is less important than maybe it is in parts of Europe or North America.
sentences.zh: 所以在这些文化中，准时可能不如在欧洲或北美部分地区那么重要。

sentences.en: There is a big contrast here. In some cultures, time is something you control and manage.
sentences.zh: 这里存在着巨大的反差。在某些文化中，时间是你可以控制和管理的东西。

sentences.en: In other cultures, time is something you experience and share.
sentences.zh: 而在另一些文化中，时间是你去体验和分享的东西。

sentences.en: According to the cultural researcher Richard D.
sentences.zh: 根据文化研究学者理查德·D·刘易斯（Richard D. Lewis）的观点，人类理解时间主要有三种方式。

sentences.en: Lewis, there are three main ways humans understand time.
sentences.zh: 它们分别是“线性时间”、“循环时间”和“程序时间”。

sentences.en: These are “linear time”, “cyclical time “, and “procedural time “.
sentences.zh: “线性”这个词用来描述某种从起点出发、沿直线前行、既不重复也不倒退的事物。

sentences.en: The word linear is used to describe something that travels in a straight line from a starting point to the end without repeating or going backwards.
sentences.zh: 想象一条直线。“循环”这个词则用来描述像一年有四季那样呈圆圈运动的事物。

sentences.en: Think of a straight line. The word cyclical describes something that moves in a circle like a year with four seasons.
sentences.zh: 季节是循环的。而“程序”指的是某种方法或一套规则。

sentences.en: The seasons are cyclical. And procedural refers to a method or set of rules.
sentences.zh: 通过这些简单的定义，你大概能猜出线性时间、循环时间，或许还有程序时间的含义，但无论如何我都会做进一步解释。

sentences.en: You might be able to guess the meanings of linear, cyclical, maybe procedural time from these simple definitions, but I’ll explain further in any case.
sentences.zh: 对于收听节目的绝大多数人来说，你们可能对“线性时间”最为熟悉。

sentences.en: For the majority of you listening, you are likely most familiar with “linear time”.
sentences.zh: 这就是时间沿直线流逝的观点。

sentences.en: This is the idea that time moves in a straight line.
sentences.zh: 它从过去出发，穿过现在，走向未来。

sentences.en: It travels from the past through the present, and into the future.
sentences.zh: 过去已经消失。现在正在发生。

sentences.en: The past is gone. The present is happening now.
sentences.zh: 而未来则是你可以规划和控制的对象。

sentences.en: And the future is something you can plan for and control.
sentences.zh: 遵循线性时间的文化往往非常关注规划、日程安排和进度，因为时间是你可以组织和管理的东西。

sentences.en: Cultures that follow linear time tend to focus a lot on things like planning and scheduling and progress, because time is something you can organize and manage.
sentences.zh: 在许多西方国家，你会听到诸如“时间就是金钱”或“不要浪费时间”这样的短语，因为我们把时间看作是一个向前推移且总量有限的东西。

sentences.en: In many Western countries, you’ll hear phrases like, “time is money” or “don’t waste time” because we see time as something moving forward that we have a limited amount of.
sentences.zh: “循环时间”则是一个截然不同的概念。

sentences.en: “Cyclical time” is a very different idea.
sentences.zh: 时间不再是一条直线，而被视为一个圆圈。

sentences.en: Instead of a straight line, time is seen as a circle.
sentences.zh: 想想大自然。白天变成黑夜，黑夜又变成白天，白天再次变成黑夜，然后又是白天。

sentences.en: Think about nature. Day turns into night, which then turns into day again, which turns into night again, and then day.
sentences.zh: 这个循环周而复始。或者春天变成夏天，接着是秋天、冬天，然后又是春天。

sentences.en: The cycle continues. Or spring becomes summer, then autumn, then winter, then spring again.
sentences.zh: 万物周而复始。在循环时间的文化中，时间并没有真正的开始或结束。

sentences.en: Things repeat. In cyclical time cultures, time doesn’t really have a beginning or end.
sentences.zh: 它只是在某种程度上不断地周而复始。

sentences.en: It just, kind of, keeps moving in cycles.
sentences.zh: 这种思维方式或许可以在受印度教或佛教等宗教影响的文化中看到。

sentences.en: This way of thinking can be seen in cultures perhaps that were influenced by religions like Hinduism or Buddhism.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个有趣的语言学例子。

sentences.en: There’s an interesting linguistic example.
sentences.zh: 在印地语中，“kal”这个词既可以指“昨天”，也可以指“明天”。

sentences.en: In Hindi, the word “kal” can mean both “yesterday” and “tomorrow “.
sentences.zh: 比如明天是未来的某一天，而昨天是过去的某一天。

sentences.en: Like tomorrow is one day in the future, and yesterday is one day in the past.
sentences.zh: 从线性时间的视角来看，“昨天”和“明天”是截然不同的两回事。

sentences.en: In a linear time perspective, “yesterday” and “tomorrow” are very different things.
sentences.zh: 但如果你把时间看作是重复循环的，它们的差异就没有那么大了。

sentences.en: But if you see time as repeating, they are less different.
sentences.zh: 它们只是距离你当前所在的时间差了一天而已。

sentences.en: They are just one day away from where you currently are.
sentences.zh: 而第三种时间概念被称为“程序时间”。

sentences.en: And the third concept of time is called “procedural time”.
sentences.zh: 这在高度发达的地区并不常见，但在澳大利亚原住民等土著群体中仍然存在。

sentences.en: This is not particularly common in highly developed places, but is still found in indigenous groups like Aboriginal Australians.
sentences.zh: 在程序时间里，你无法度量时间，也无法为之做计划。

sentences.en: In procedural time, you can’t measure time or plan for it.
sentences.zh: 它既不呈直线运行，也不呈圆圈运动。

sentences.en: It doesn’t travel in a line or a circle.
sentences.zh: 相反，时间是通过事件和行动来理解的。

sentences.en: Instead, time is understood through events and actions.
sentences.zh: 只有当事情发生时，时间才存在。这听起来可能让人很困惑，但举几个例子也许会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Time only exists when things happen. This probably sounds really confusing, but maybe some examples will help.
sentences.zh: 如果我问你，“夏天是什么时候？”，你会怎么回答？

sentences.en: If I asked you, “when is summer?”, what would you answer?
sentences.zh: 线性文化中的人可能会回答七月和八月（如果你在北半球的话）。

sentences.en: People in a linear culture might answer July and August (if you’re in the Northern Hemisphere).
sentences.zh: 我们说七月和八月，因为日程表上就是这么定的。

sentences.en: We say July and August,’cause that’s what it is on the schedule.
sentences.zh: 我们可以为它做计划。循环文化中的人可能会说，在春天之后、秋天之前。

sentences.en: We can plan for it. People in a cyclical culture might say after spring, before autumn.
sentences.zh: 但程序文化中的人可能会说，“雨停之后”、“某朵特定的花盛开的时候”，或者“河水干涸的时候”。

sentences.en: But people in a procedural culture would say something like, “after the rain stops” or “when a specific flower blooms”, or “when the river is dry”.
sentences.zh: 程序时间是对真实事件、真实事物的反应，而不是对抽象概念的反应。

sentences.en: Procedural time is in response to real events, real things, not ideas.
sentences.zh: 七月和春天只是一种概念。月份和季节是词汇和观念。

sentences.en: July and spring are just ideas. Months and seasons are words and concepts.
sentences.zh: 它们不是真实存在的实体。你摸不到七月。

sentences.en: They’re not real things. You can’t touch July.
sentences.zh: 你也摸不到春天。但你能摸到雨水，能闻到花香，能去感受、看到或体验，这就是程序时间。

sentences.en: You can’t touch spring. But you can touch rain, you can smell flowers, you can feel or see or experience, and so that’s procedural time.
sentences.zh: 时间是通过对正在发生的真实事件的反应来度量的。

sentences.en: Time is measured in response to real events that are happening.
sentences.zh: 一件事发生在另一件事之后。好了，让我们抛开这些时间理论，转而思考人们是如何利用时间来安排日常生活的。

sentences.en: Something happens after something else. Okay, let’s move on from these theories of time and instead think about how people use time to organize their days.
sentences.zh: 文化之间最大的差异之一就是所谓的“时钟时间”与“事件时间”。

sentences.en: One of the biggest differences between cultures is something called “clock time” versus “event time”.
sentences.zh: 时钟时间是你们当中许多人所习惯的。

sentences.en: Clock time is what many of you will be used to.
sentences.zh: 这意味着一切都是按照日程表来安排的。

sentences.en: It means that everything is organized according to schedules.
sentences.zh: 如果一个会议定在早上9:00开始，那它就会在早上9:00准时开始。

sentences.en: If a meeting starts at 9:00 AM it starts at 9:00 AM.
sentences.zh: 不是9:05，也不是9:10，正好是早上9:00。时间被划分为分钟和小时，每一项活动在一天中都有其固定的位置。

sentences.en: Not 9:05, not 9:10, exactly 9:00 AM. Time is divided into minutes and hours, and each activity has a place in the day.
sentences.zh: 这种方法在许多西方国家以及日本非常普遍，在这些地方，守时被看得极其重要。

sentences.en: This approach is common in many Western countries and also in Japan, where punctuality is taken very seriously.
sentences.zh: 事情在固定的时间发生，如果活动、会议或公交车迟到了，就会被视为不够专业或缺乏条理。

sentences.en: Things happen at a fixed time, and if the event or the meeting or the bus is late, it’s seems as unprofessional or disorganized.
sentences.zh: 现在再来想想事件时间。在事件时间的文化中，日程安排往往更具灵活性。

sentences.en: Now think about event time. In event time cultures, schedules tend to be more flexible.
sentences.zh: 会议或派对会在每个人都准备好时开始，而不是在一个固定的时间。

sentences.en: A meeting or a party will start when everyone is ready, not at a fixed time.
sentences.zh: 所以它是基于事件本身，而不是基于时钟。

sentences.en: So it’s based on the event, not on the clock.
sentences.zh: 我想，活动会根据具体情况更加自然地开始和结束。

sentences.en: I guess activities begin and end more naturally depending on the situation.
sentences.zh: 这在亚洲部分地区、非洲部分地区以及拉丁美洲部分地区很常见。

sentences.en: This is common in parts of Asia, parts of Africa, parts of Latin America.
sentences.zh: “时钟时间”与“事件时间”的不同，正是国际会议和活动中为什么有些人显得迟到或早到、或者事情脱离计划的主要原因之一。

sentences.en: “Clock time” versus “event time” is one of the main reasons why some people seem late or early, or things go off schedule in international meetings and events.
sentences.zh: 文化不同的另一个重要方面被称为“时间取向”。

sentences.en: Another important way in which cultures differ is something called “time orientation”.
sentences.zh: 时间取向指的是一种文化更喜欢关注时间的哪一部分：过去、现在还是未来。

sentences.en: Time orientation refers to which part of time a culture likes to focus on: the past, the present, or the future.
sentences.zh: 在面向过去的文化中，人们高度珍视他们的传统。

sentences.en: In past-oriented cultures, people place a strong value on their traditions.
sentences.zh: 他们经常思考历史，并遵循既定的行事方式。

sentences.en: They think a lot about history, and they follow established ways of doing things.
sentences.zh: 遵循你们的风俗，遵循你们的传统。

sentences.en: Follow your customs, follow your traditions.
sentences.zh: 有些人把英国描述为面向过去的文化，或者中国可能也是。

sentences.en: Some people describe the UK as a past-oriented culture or maybe China Present-oriented cultures focus on now.
sentences.zh: 面向现在的文化则专注于当下。

sentences.en: Rather than thinking too much about the past or planning too much for the future, people focus on their immediate needs and their current experiences.
sentences.zh: 比起过多地思考过去或为未来做过多规划，人们更关注眼前的需求和当前的体验。

sentences.en: People say some parts of Latin America and Africa are present-oriented cultures.
sentences.zh: 人们说拉丁美洲和非洲的某些部分是面向现在的文化。

sentences.en: And future-oriented cultures are focused on their goals, planning and progress.
sentences.zh: 而面向未来的文化则专注于他们的目标、规划和进步。

sentences.en: The United States is the classic example.
sentences.zh: 美国就是一个典型的例子。

sentences.en: People spend a lot of time thinking about what they want to achieve in the future, how to organize their lives, and how to improve their future.
sentences.zh: 人们花大量时间思考未来想取得什么成就、如何安排生活以及如何改善未来。

sentences.en: The anthropologist Edward T. Hall introduced another useful way of distinguishing between cultures.
sentences.zh: 人类学家爱德华·T·霍尔（Edward T. Hall）提出了另一种区分文化的有用方法。

sentences.en: ” Monochronic” and “polychronic” time. Monochronic and polychronic sound confusing, but if you look at the parts of the word the meaning is clear.
sentences.zh: 即“单向时间”与“多向时间”。单向时间和多向时间听起来让人迷惑，但如果你拆解这些词汇的词根，意思就很清晰了。

sentences.en: Chronic is derived from the Greek “kronos” and means “related to time”.
sentences.zh: “chronic”源自希腊语“kronos”，意思是“与时间相关的”。

sentences.en: While “mono” and “poly” are prefixes, meaning one and many respectively.
sentences.zh: 而“mono”和“poly”是前缀，分别代表“单”和“多”。

sentences.en: In monochronic time, “mono” means one. So this way of thinking is all about doing one thing at a time.
sentences.zh: 在单向时间中，“mono”意为单一。所以这种思维方式的核心是一次只做一件事。

sentences.en: People in monochronic cultures follow a schedule and plan their day carefully.
sentences.zh: 单向时间文化中的人遵循日程表，仔细规划他们的一天。

sentences.en: You do one task after another. One thing at a time.
sentences.zh: 你一个接一个地完成任务。一次只做一件事。

sentences.en: Countries like Germany and the United States are examples, and Japan as well is strongly monochronic, especially in business.
sentences.zh: 像德国和美国就是这样的例子，日本也是强烈的单向时间文化，尤其是在商业领域。

sentences.en: With monochronic time, workplaces will focus on productivity and punctuality and finishing your work before you start the next project.
sentences.zh: 在单向时间下，工作场所会专注于生产力、守时，并且在开始下一个项目之前先完成手头的工作。

sentences.en: Polychronic cultures are the opposite. “Poly” means many, so people are comfortable doing multiple things at the same time.
sentences.zh: 多向时间文化则恰恰相反。“Poly”意为多，所以人们习惯于同时做多件事情。

sentences.en: Multitasking is very common in polychronic cultures.
sentences.zh: 多任务处理在多向时间文化中非常普遍。

sentences.en: People do multiple tasks at the same time.
sentences.zh: 人们同时处理多项任务。

sentences.en: Time is more flexible and less predictable.
sentences.zh: 时间更具灵活性，也更难以预测。

sentences.en: Events can be rescheduled, meetings can be changed, and there’s a lot more group involvement.
sentences.zh: 活动可以重新安排，会议可以更改，并且有更多的群体参与。

sentences.en: So now that we’ve looked at lots of different ways of understanding time, what happens when these different understandings, these different time systems, meet?
sentences.zh: 所以，既然我们已经探讨了这么多理解时间的不同方式，那么当这些不同的理解、这些不同的时间系统相遇时会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: Imagine you’re invited to a party that starts at 7:00 PM.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，你受邀去参加一个晚上7:00开始的派对。

sentences.en: What time would you arrive? Well, I’m British.
sentences.zh: 你会在几点到达？嗯，我是英国人。

sentences.en: I come from quite a punctual, schedule focused culture.
sentences.zh: 我来自一个相当守时、注重日程安排的文化背景。

sentences.en: I would probably arrive at 6:55 and wait outside.
sentences.zh: 我大概会在6:55到达并在外面等待。

sentences.en: And then knock on the door exactly at 7:00 PM.
sentences.zh: 然后正好在晚上7:00敲门。

sentences.en: But if you come from a culture with a different understanding of time, you might not arrive until 8:00 PM or 9:00 PM or later.
sentences.zh: 但如果你来自一个对时间有不同理解的文化背景，你可能直到晚上8:00、9:00甚至更晚才会出现。

sentences.en: And depending on where the host is from, the host of the party, they might be expecting the party to start exactly at 7:00 PM or start much later.
sentences.zh: 这还要看主人来自哪里，派对的主人可能期望派对准时在晚上7:00开始，或者晚得多才开始。

sentences.en: I actually have a great example of when different time cultures clash.
sentences.zh: 我其实有一个很好的例子，关于不同的时间文化是如何发生冲突的。

sentences.en: When I lived in Tokyo a few years ago, a Japanese friend invited me and two other friends to eat sushi together.
sentences.zh: 几年前我住在东京时，一个日本朋友邀请我和另外两个朋友一起去吃寿司。

sentences.en: My two friends were from Fiji in the Pacific and the Ivory Coast in Africa.
sentences.zh: 我的两个朋友一个来自太平洋的斐济，另一个来自非洲的科特迪瓦。

sentences.en: We agreed to meet at 5:00 PM at a train station near where we lived.
sentences.zh: 我们商定下午5:00在我们住处附近的一个火车站见面。

sentences.en: I turned up at the train station at 4:50PM and met my Japanese friend at exactly 5:00 PM.
sentences.zh: 我在下午4:50到达火车站，并在刚好5:00见到了我的日本朋友。

sentences.en: We sat outside the station waiting. About 45 minutes later, so 45 minutes late, my Fijian friend joined.
sentences.zh: 我们坐在车站外面等待。大约45分钟后，也就是迟到了45分钟，我的斐济朋友来了。

sentences.en: By the time it got to 6:00 PM we hadn’t heard from the friend from Ivory Coast, so we went to eat sushi, and then we went to a local bar where we had actually all met each other in the past.
sentences.zh: 到了傍晚6:00，我们依然没有收到来自科特迪瓦朋友的任何消息，于是我们去吃了寿司，然后去了一家本地酒吧——我们过去其实就是在那家酒吧认识彼此的。

sentences.en: At 9:00 PM, the friend from the Ivory Coast finally arrived.
sentences.zh: 晚上9:00，那位科特迪瓦的朋友终于到了。

sentences.en: I was focused on the schedule and my Japanese friend were focused on the schedule.
sentences.zh: 我和我的日本朋友都专注于日程安排。

sentences.en: 5:00 PM was the time that we were going to meet, and I organized my day around reaching the station at 5:00 PM.
sentences.zh: 下午5:00是我们原本要碰面的时间，我围绕着在下午5:00到达车站来安排我的一天。

sentences.en: So did my Japanese friend. But my friends from Fiji and the Ivory Coast had events in their day that they had organized around.
sentences.zh: 我的日本朋友也是如此。但我来自斐济和科特迪瓦的朋友则是围绕着他们当天的其他事件来安排时间的。

sentences.en: It’s just a different perspective on time.
sentences.zh: 这只是一种对时间的不同视角。

sentences.en: In countries like Japan, the UK, Germany, Switzerland, being on time is important.
sentences.zh: 在像日本、英国、德国、瑞士这样的国家，守时非常重要。

sentences.en: In fact, arriving exactly on time can sometimes feel like you are late.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正好准时到达有时会让你觉得好像自己迟到了。

sentences.en: Many people including me, aim to arrive early.
sentences.zh: 包括我在内的许多人，目标都是提前到达。

sentences.en: From my perspective being punctual shows respect.
sentences.zh: 从我的角度来看，守时表示尊重。

sentences.en: What if the event starts exactly on time?
sentences.zh: 如果活动准时开始怎么办？

sentences.en: But in other parts of the world, Fiji or the Ivory Coast, or perhaps Brazil, India, time tends to be a bit more flexible.
sentences.zh: 但在世界的其他地方，比如斐济、科特迪瓦，或者巴西、印度，时间往往要灵活一些。

sentences.en: Arriving late might be normal and not considered rude.
sentences.zh: 迟到可能是正常的，并不被认为是不礼貌的。

sentences.en: In some cases, arriving too early can be rude and arriving too early can be awkward.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，到得太早反而才是不礼貌的，而且会很尴尬。

sentences.en: This same behavior, “being late “, can have completely different meanings depending on the culture.
sentences.zh: 同样的“迟到”行为，根据文化的不同，可能会有完全截然相反的含义。

sentences.en: In monochronic cultures waiting is sometimes seen as a problem.
sentences.zh: 在单向时间的文化中，等待有时被视为一个问题。

sentences.en: If you have to wait for someone, for a meeting to start, or for an event to begin, it feels like you’re losing time.
sentences.zh: 如果你不得不等某个人、等一场会议开始、或者等一个活动开场，你会觉得自己浪费了时间。

sentences.en: But in polychronic cultures, waiting tends to be a bit more accepted.
sentences.zh: 但在多向时间的文化中，等待往往更能被接受。

sentences.en: Waiting can also be connected to your status.
sentences.zh: 等待也可能与你的社会地位挂钩。

sentences.en: The more important or the more powerful you are, the more you might keep other people waiting.
sentences.zh: 你越重要、越有权势，你可能就越会让别人等你。

sentences.en: So it’s not always negative, it can just have different social meanings.
sentences.zh: 所以它并不总是负面的，只是有着不同的社会含义。

sentences.en: The title of this podcast episode is probably something like, “Why are Some People Always Late?” I’ve not decided yet.
sentences.zh: 这个播客节目的标题大概会类似于“为什么有些人总是迟到？”我还没完全决定。

sentences.en: It’s likely this title. So let me try to answer that question.
sentences.zh: 很可能就是这个标题。所以让我试着回答这个问题。

sentences.en: If I invited you to a party at 8:00 PM and you turned up exactly at 8:00 or earlier, you are probably from a culture that is more linear in how you see time and more monochronic.
sentences.zh: 如果我邀请你在晚上8:00参加派对，而你正好在8:00或更早到场，你大概来自一个对时间的看法更偏向线性、且更倾向于单向时间的文化。

sentences.en: In your culture, being early or on time is a way of being respectful and professional.
sentences.zh: 在你的文化中，早到或准时是一种表达尊重和专业的方式。

sentences.en: You also likely look at the clock to schedule your day.
sentences.zh: 你很可能也通过看时钟来安排你的一天。

sentences.en: If you turned up to my party late, you might come from a culture that understands time in a more cyclical or event-based way.
sentences.zh: 如果你迟到了我的派对，你可能来自一个以更循环或更基于事件的方式理解时间的文化。

sentences.en: Your time may be more present-oriented or polychronic.
sentences.zh: 你的时间观念可能更偏向现在、或者是多向时间的。

sentences.en: If you arrive late, maybe it’s not a problem in your culture.
sentences.zh: 如果你迟到了，在你的文化里这或许根本不是个问题。

sentences.en: Maybe it’s expected. Maybe people will understand you were doing something else instead.
sentences.zh: 也许这本就是意料之中。也许大家会理解你当时正在忙别的事。

sentences.en: Your schedule is just less fixed. Once you understand this, once you understand that different cultures have different understandings of time, it becomes much easier to be flexible and less frustrated when people behave differently.
sentences.zh: 你的日程安排没那么死板。一旦你明白了这一点，一旦你理解了不同的文化对时间有着不同的理解，当人们表现出不同行为时，你就更容易保持灵活性，也就不会那么沮丧了。

sentences.en: It can also make it easier for you to communicate.
sentences.zh: 这也能让你们的沟通变得更加顺畅。

sentences.en: If you know someone who comes from a culture that really focuses on punctuality, being on time, well then make an effort to turn up exactly at that time.
sentences.zh: 如果你认识一个来自非常注重守时、准时文化的某个人，那么就努力准时在那个时间出现吧。

sentences.en: Or if you know someone comes from a culture that’s a bit more flexible, a bit less concerned about the exact time on the clock, maybe go to the party a few minutes late, rather than early like I would.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你知道某人来自一个更灵活、对时钟上的精确时间没那么介意的文化，或许去派对时稍微迟到几分钟，而不是像我那样提前到。

sentences.en: This episode has tried to take a look at different cultural understandings of time.
sentences.zh: 本期节目尝试探讨了不同文化对时间的理解。

sentences.en: We saw how different cultures understand the direction of time, how different cultures use time differently, how different cultures look at the past or the present or the future, and how all of this can create challenges and misunderstandings.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了不同的文化如何理解时间的流逝方向，不同的文化如何以不同方式使用时间，不同的文化如何看待过去、现在或未来，以及所有这些如何带来挑战和误解。

sentences.en: Right at the beginning of the episode, I asked you a question.
sentences.zh: 就在节目的刚开始，我问了你一个问题。

sentences.en: You are invited to a party. The invitation says the party starts at 8:00 PM.
sentences.zh: 你受邀去参加一个派对。邀请函上写着派对在晚上8:00开始。

sentences.en: What time will you arrive? I want to know your answer.
sentences.zh: 你会在几点到达？我想知道你的答案。

sentences.en: And maybe what would the average person from your culture or your country do?
sentences.zh: 而且，你觉得你们文化或国家里的普通人会怎么做？

sentences.en: Would you arrive at 8:00 PM? 7:45PM? 9:00 PM?
And what do you think that says about your culture?
sentences.zh: 你认为这说明了你们文化的什么特点呢？
